summary: Tested the separate Admin Panel auth in the backend (31 new pytest cases plus 21 updated iter38 push/location regression tests) and in the UI with Playwright (admin login, auto-login, protected routes, tabs, logout, no admin entry point for normal users). Every requested feature works. Two security gaps found: (1) a spoofed X-Forwarded-For header bypasses the admin login rate limit; (2) the special branch for ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD in /api/auth/login has no rate limit, so the admin password can be brute-forced there, and the regular account it creates keeps is_admin=True privileges on user endpoints.

critical.issue: Rate limiting is per IP, and the IP comes from the FIRST X-Forwarded-For entry, which the client controls. After 5 fails (locked, 429), the same client sent 'X-Forwarded-For: 10.9.x.7' and got 200 plus a token. The backend log showed 'admin login from 10.9.223.7'. Brute force is effectively unlimited (only the 1s delay remains, and it can be run in parallel).

routers/auth.py has a special branch that compares body.password == ADMIN_PASSWORD (plain ==, not hmac) and has no rate limit or lockout. The admin panel password can be brute-forced through the normal login endpoint, then used on /admin/login.

minor.issue: Logging in to the normal app as admin@lovreski.ru returns a user JWT with is_admin=True, and the DB user has is_admin=True. That account can still delete any chat message for everyone with no 1-hour window (chat.py:122-140), read any private file such as payment receipts (files.py:62), run /demo/seed and message for free. /api/admin/* is correctly blocked (401). This conflicts with the user's choice that a normal login must not grant admin powers.
Lockout is per IP only. Preview egress IPs alternate (35.196.x / 136.108.x), so the counter splits across IPs. Consider also keeping a global counter for the admin email.

issues: Date of birth uses the browser's native date input instead of the shadcn calendar (existing behaviour, not part of this change)

passed_items: POST /api/admin/login: correct credentials -> {success:true, token}; email is case-insensitive; wrong email or password -> 401 'Invalid email or password' after a delay of at least 0.9s; empty fields -> 422
Same IP: 5 fails -> 6th attempt with the correct password gets 429 'Too many failed attempts...'
verify-token: valid -> {valid:true}; missing, garbage or forged token (correct secret but no session jti) -> 401
User JWTs (normal login of admin@lovreski.ru and of testuser1) -> 401 on verify-token, stats, push/config, users, settings
Admin token -> 200 on 14 admin GET routes (stats, payments, users, settings, support x3, push/config, legal, storage, storage/cleanup-log, refunds, reports, audit); no token -> 401
Admin token has no exp claim; type=admin; logout revokes it (verify-token and stats -> 401 afterwards); other sessions stay valid

UI: /admin and /admin/dashboard without a token -> /admin/login; wrong credentials show the error and stay on the page with no token stored; correct credentials -> /admin/dashboard with lovreski_admin_token set
UI: reloading the dashboard or revisiting /admin/login while logged in skips the form; /admin/whatever -> dashboard; all 9 tabs click with no failed /api/admin calls; Push tab renders
UI: logout clears the token and goes to /admin/login; revisiting /admin/dashboard asks for login again
UI: normal login of admin@lovreski.ru and of testuser1 lands on /home; Settings and Profile have no admin button or link; /admin/dashboard as a normal user -> /admin/login
Admin credentials are not in the frontend bundle or in src
action_items: Fix how admin_auth._client_ip picks the client IP: do not trust the first X-Forwarded-For entry. Take the right-most hop added by the trusted ingress (or request.client.host behind a known proxy), and/or add a global failure counter for ADMIN_EMAIL so spoofing the IP cannot bypass the lockout

Remove the ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD special branch from /api/auth/login, or give it the same rate limit, use hmac.compare_digest and do not mint is_admin=True user tokens. Ideally add rate limiting to /api/auth/login for all users

Decide whether the admin@lovreski.ru normal account should keep is_admin=True privileges on user endpoints (chat delete-any, files access-any, demo seed). Per the user's choice it probably should not; drive these privileges from the admin JWT or remove the flag
critical_code_review_comments: routers/auth.py login: plaintext == comparison against ADMIN_PASSWORD with no lockout; the special branch duplicates the admin path
verify_admin looks up the user by ADMIN_EMAIL and returns that document, so admin actions are recorded under the regular user_id (fine, but this couples the two)
The admin_sessions collection grows forever (no TTL or cleanup of revoked sessions); minor
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_push_location_iter38.py (admin fixture now uses /api/admin/login; user-token checks on admin routes now expect 401 instead of 403)

success_rate.backend: 96% (50/52 in a parallel run; the lockout test passes when run serially; the X-Forwarded-For spoof test fails = real security bug)

test_credentials: From /app/memory/test_credentials.md: admin admin@lovreski.ru / LovreskiAdmin2026! (via /admin/login); testuser1@lovreski.ru / password123
seed_data_creation: None. admin_login_attempts was reset (deleteMany) after the rate-limit tests; count is 0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the rate-limit tests serially: pytest test_admin_auth_iter39.py -k rate_limit -o addopts="". pytest.ini enables xdist, and parallel successful logins clear the per-IP fail record. Always run db.admin_login_attempts.deleteMany({}) afterwards. iter38 tests now use the admin token.
rca of the issue: Rate-limit bypass: _client_ip returns x-forwarded-for.split(',')[0], which the client controls (the ingress appends the real IP to the right). Reproduce: send 5 bad passwords, then the correct password with the header 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4' -> 200. A second brute-force path exists through /api/auth/login's admin special-case, which has no limiter.
